# Template: rd_plot
A regression-discontinuity plot: binned scatter dots on both sides of a cutoff, separate fitted lines left and right, a dashed vertical line at the cutoff, and a bracket marking the jump — the treatment effect. Choose this scene for ANY request about regression discontinuity, RD or RDD designs, cutoffs and running variables, thresholds that assign treatment (test scores, age limits, income lines), or the jump at a discontinuity.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "jump": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "The discontinuity at the cutoff, -4..4 (default 2)."
  },
  "slope": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Underlying slope, -0.5..0.5 (default 0.22)."
  },
  "curvature": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Underlying curvature, -0.03..0.03 (default 0.012)."
  },
  "noise": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Vertical scatter of the binned dots, 0-1 (default 0.32)."
  },
  "x_label": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "The running variable (default \"Running variable\")."
  },
  "cutoff_label": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Caption on the cutoff line (default \"Cutoff\")."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string"
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- axes: the coordinate axes (a group with captions)
- dots_left: binned scatter dots left of the cutoff (a group; dots_right likewise)
- dots_right: binned dots right of the cutoff
- fit_left: fitted line left of the cutoff (fit_right likewise)
- fit_right: fitted line right of the cutoff
- cutoff_line: dashed vertical line at the cutoff (with caption)
- jump_bracket: double arrow marking the jump, with its caption
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Draw a regression discontinuity plot with a clear jump at the cutoff." → params: {"title":"Regression discontinuity"}
Request: "Show an RD design where crossing the threshold lowers the outcome." → params: {"jump":-1.8,"title":"A penalty at the threshold"}

In YAML: `template: rd_plot` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
